In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adenosinetriphosphate effect is a part of an ATP conservation system which is superposed on product feedback control.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rate of ATP consumption by a biosynthetic pathway is not simply proportional to the rate of synthesis of its product.
the rate of ATP consumption by a biosynthetic enzyme can be regulated by a combination of product negative feedback and ATP conservation.
the rate of synthesis of phosphoribosyll-pyrophosphate is regulated both by the energy charge of E. coli and by the concentration of tryptophan in it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the enzyme is regulated by a combination of product inhibition, adenosine tri-phosphate conservation, and allosteric inhibition.
ATP conservation is a general feature of metabolic control in Escherichia. coli, which is not limited to the purine nucleotide cycle.

the ATP conservation effect on phosphoribosly-pyrophosphate (PRPP) synthase may be a general phenomenon, and that the enzyme is not the only enzyme in the purine nucleotide biosynthetic pathway subject to ATP conservation control.
